title: Warner Music Group Yearly Revenue Rises 9% on Streaming, Digital Growth
summary: CEO Robert Kyncl says "durable" market share gains and releases like the soundtrack to the new Grand Theft Auto game will drive growth in fiscal 2027.
contentText:
Warner Music Group said on Thursday (Nov. 19) revenue for its full fiscal year rose by nearly 9% to $7.4 billion, driven by double-digit growth in digital and streaming revenue.

The company reported revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter ending Sept. 30 rose 7.5% in constant currency thanks to accelerated growth in recorded music division stemming from releases like Madonna ’s 15th studio album, Confessions II and Charli XCX ’s Music, Fashion, Film.

Increases in streaming subscription prices at Apple Music and other streamers and the acquisition of digital music distributor Revelator added to WMG’s full-year revenue growth, but CEO Robert Kyncl expressed optimism that “durable” gains in market share and reduced costs will result in a repeat performance in fiscal 2027.

“Our [fiscal fourth quarter] and full-year results demonstrate the success of a multiyear, transformational strategy that sets a new bar for WMG,” Kyncl said in a statement. New releases like Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , the soundtrack featuring artists including Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Lana Del Rey, Gunna and Morgan Wallen, alongside the WMG’s “tech-enabled capabilities, position us to drive sustainable, long-term value for our artists, songwriters and shareholders in fiscal 2027 and beyond,” Kyncl said.

WMG’s multiyear restructuring plan, which cut annual costs by $300 million through a combination of executive changes , layoffs and reduced expenses, contributed to fourth-quarter operating income rising by a whopping $177 million to $320 million. This 122% increase from the year-ago quarter included a $107 million reduction in restructuring and noncash impairment charges.

Warner Music Group Announces Major Executive Restructure, Max Lousada to Step Down

Full fiscal year operating income grew by almost 70% to $1.18 billion from $694 million, driven by a shift in the company’s revenue mix, savings from restructuring and higher adjusted operating income before depreciation and amortization (OIBDA). Adjusted OIBDA rose 19.4% in constant currency to $1.8 billion, and adjusted OIBDA margin, a key metric to measure shareholder value, grew 2.1 percentage points to 21.7% in constant currency.

Cash from the company’s operating activities rose 28% to $866 million as the company’s performance offset payments related to restructuring and contractual digital advances. Operating cash flow conversion was 49% of Adjusted OIBDA. Executives are targeting 50-60% margins in fiscal 2027.

The company’s stock was down 2.25% in mid-day trading in New York.

Full-year digital revenue increased 10.4% in constant currency, and streaming revenue increased 11.2% in constant currency. Full-year recorded music revenue grew by 11% to $5.99 billion, with recorded music streaming revenue growing by 13.5% despite a $29 million headwind from the termination of BMG’s distribution deal. Within the recorded music division, digital revenue contributed $4.04 billion in revenue, with physical up to $593 million. Full-year music publishing revenue rose to $1.46 billion, with music publishing streaming revenue up 13.9%. Overall digital publishing revenue drove $905 million, up from $800 million the year prior.

Looking just at the fourth quarter, recorded music revenue rose 7.3%, and music publishing revenue rose 7.4% from a year ago. Company-wide fourth-quarter streaming rose 13.7%, with streaming revenue for recorded music rising 13.4% increase, and streaming revenue from music publishing revenue up 15.1%.

Fourth-quarter adjusted OIBDA grew by 17.2% to $477 million, and adjusted OIBDA margin grew by nearly two percentage points to 23.8% on the increased operating income and the savings from restructuring, “a portion of which has been reinvested into the company’s business,” according to WMG.
